title: LightMood Intervention to reduce depression symptoms in obese adults: A randomized-controlled online intervention study
summary: Due to the high prevalence of obese people worldwide suffering from physical and psychological stress, the treatment of such patients requires high frequency long-term care. The prospective randomized controlled trial aims to evaluate the efficacy of the LightMood intervention. The term LightMood is composed of the terms Light and Mood, which is a manualized, electronic training for obese patients that includes elements of cognitive behavioral therapy. In this study, we expect the LightMood intervention to be superior to treatment as usual (TAU) in reducing depressive symptoms.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
-Patients with a BMI ≥ 30
-Depressive symptoms (PHQ-8 ≥ 10)
-Adequate digital literacy
-Internet-enabled device
-Informed consent
Exclusion criteria:
-Bariatric surgery within the past year or planned within the next 6 months
-Weekly individual psychotherapy
-No private Internet access
-Regulation of a new psychopharmacists within the last 2 weeks
